planApproval.note: Graduated 'required' -> 'auto' by the user, 2026-08-01 (see review-feedback: review-gate-graduation). /plan-issue posts the plan and proceeds to /execute, EXCEPT: plans for issues carrying any label in alwaysRequiredFor STILL stop for user approval — ADRs are major decisions and the user steers at this altitude — and any plan whose Risks section contains a question only the user can answer stops and surfaces it.
planApproval.debtBurn: Issues labelled 'debt-burn' skip plan approval: the issue body IS the plan (triage only applies the label to small, proven, well-scoped work with named files and mechanical acceptance). Anything needing a re-structure or re-think is not labelled debt-burn and keeps the full gates.

merge.autoRule: A PR auto-merges once CI is green iff it contains NO source-code files AND touches nothing under humanAlways paths. Source code = extensions .ts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .sh .py .tf .sql — files whose structure (functions, modules, components) the user reviews. Markdown, JSON, YAML, and other plain config auto-merge.
merge.reviewedSourceRule: A source-code PR auto-merges once CI is green AND an independent reviewer pass ended in APPROVE — /review-loop's, or the ticket-agent lane's single targeted `reviewer` pass (.claude/agents/ticket-agent.md rule 6) — unless it touches a humanAlways path. SELF-REVIEW NEVER SATISFIES THIS RULE: what the gate buys is a reader who did not write the diff, and an author who dispatches that reader has not read their own work. Owner decision 2026-09-10 (#468), verbatim: 'an independent `reviewer` pass dispatched by the ticket-agent (one targeted cycle + confirmation on fix commits) satisfies `merge.reviewedSourceRule`; self-review never does'. Graduated by the user 2026-08-01 (see review-feedback: review-gate-graduation) — the generalisation of debtBurnRule and refactorRule (deleted from this file in the same 2026-08-10 revision; its calibration record lives on as the `2026-07-31 — refactor-lane` entry in docs/review-feedback.md) after every source PR this stretch (#95 #97 #114 #116 #119 #121 #124 #130 #131 #132) merged on exactly that evidence. The APPROVE is the load-bearing gate: no APPROVE, no merge, regardless of CI.
merge.humanAlwaysRule: PRs touching a humanAlways path: the docs/review-feedback.md entry goes on the branch FIRST (mergeRitual owns what it must say), then CI green, then label 'awaiting-review' — whose own fresh run stays green, the entry already being in the diff — then notify the user with a short review guide, do NOT merge (chat approval from the user also unblocks); continue with independent tickets while it waits. That order is load-bearing, not preference: labelling before the entry exists reddens mergeRitualGate by construction, and a red gate leaves no ready PR to notify on. ADRs decide direction; workflow.json and CLAUDE.md ARE the gates — they never pass through the gates they define.
merge.mergeRitual: A PR that carries 'awaiting-review' logs its own review-feedback line ON THE BRANCH, before the label goes on: the docs/review-feedback.md entry is part of the diff the owner approves, written in the form that file's `## Entry format` section declares. That declaration owns both halves — what the entry says before the label, and what whoever merges fills at merge (the Verdict, and the Category it fixes) — so this key restates neither. Merge-time order, and it is load-bearing: the Verdict is filled ON THE BRANCH (it is a branch commit, so necessarily before the merge), THEN the PR merges, THEN the label comes off — nothing is owed after that. Label removal goes last because `on:` in .github/workflows/ci.yml is workflow-level, so every label event re-runs every job; that file's merge-ritual-gate comment block accepts the resulting run against a just-merged PR as the known-harmless edge, whereas unlabelling first spends a full CI round on a still-open PR that the merge owner would then have to settle before merging. Moved from after-merge to on-branch 2026-08-10 after PR #345 omitted the line while its body claimed it, and PR #348 deferred its own line to a later PR — a step owed after the merge is a step no gate can block; provisional form (the ask before the label, the verdict at merge) adopted 2026-08-11 per #409. A quiet feedback category must be distinguishable from an unlogged one, or nothing can ever graduate; this ritual is what made reviewedSourceRule graduatable.
merge.mergeRitualGate: Mechanical half: a CI check fails any PR labelled 'awaiting-review' whose diff does not touch docs/review-feedback.md. Wire it into .github/workflows/ci.yml as its own job (not into `pnpm verify`, which knows nothing about labels). The check is a floor, not a proof — it cannot tell a good entry from a placeholder — which is why the prose half above still owns what the entry must say.
merge.debtBurnRule: A PR closing a 'debt-burn'-labelled issue auto-merges once CI is green AND the review loop ended in APPROVE, even when it touches source code. Decided by the user 2026-07-30 (see review-feedback: debt-burn-lane). Subsumed by reviewedSourceRule 2026-08-01 but kept as the planApproval half's anchor: debt-burn also skips plan approval.
merge.note: Further relaxation (or tightening after a bad merge) is proposed via retro PR — the user decides. A merge later shown to be wrong reverts via a plain revert PR and gets a review-feedback entry naming what the review loop missed.

orchestration.routeRule: The ticket SET's shape picks the lane, and nothing else does. A SINGLE ISSUE runs in the TICKET-AGENT lane: one ticket-agent (.claude/agents/ticket-agent.md) owns it end to end in its own worktree, dispatched per .claude/skills/run-issue/SKILL.md. Every single issue, with no size tier at admission — owner decision 2026-09-10 (#468), verbatim: 'All single issues take the lane; the agent's plan-time one-honest-PR stop replaces a size tier.' A MULTI-TICKET SAME-SURFACE BATCH — 2-6 members meeting run-issue's composition test, unchanged — still runs DELEGATED: one task-orchestrator per batch via /run-issue, one agent, one in-flight row, one plan. The two exceptions that used to send a single issue delegated are deleted: the lane's own context is now the budget the top-level's context used to be. The one in-lane escape is the agent's plan-time 'BLOCKED — needs splitting' (.claude/agents/ticket-agent.md rule 2), which the top-level answers by splitting the issue or composing a batch — a tier chosen at admission is a prediction made before anyone has read the files, and that stop is a measurement made after. The top-level session owns merging and merge-readiness in every lane. Rationale in costEvidence; what each lane still owes is in delegatedContract.
orchestration.costEvidence: BASELINE — session-observed accounting over the 2026-08-10 runs, and the reason the lane is shape-routed rather than universal. Single-ticket delegated runs cost ~700-900k tokens per ticket against ~400k for comparable inline-orchestrated tickets — roughly double for the same ticket, for no measured quality gain. The six-ticket same-surface design batch amortised to ~220k per ticket, i.e. BELOW inline, because the per-set fixed overhead (dispatch, plan transmission, checkpoint, report, handover) is paid once by a batch and once per ticket by a single issue. Orchestrator contexts ended at 230-310k. Part of the gap was operational rather than structural and is fixed rather than priced in: ~25 sub-agent completion notifications mis-routed to the top-level session and hand-relayed (fix: synchronous dispatch inside orchestrators), and interim narration between orchestrator and top-level (fix: reports only at contract checkpoints). The machine-local budget ledger at the time of the decision read 5h window at 100% of limit, 7d at 32.9%, mode 'conserve' — the cost is a live constraint, not an abstraction. TICKET-AGENT PILOT — the two tickets that ran in the lane's shape before it was a lane, quoted verbatim from the #468 comment of 2026-08-25: '#463 ≈ 168k tokens / 94 tool uses / 29 min; #459 ≈ 133k / 65 / 30 min — run concurrently, so ~30 min wall-clock for both.' Two touchpoints each, zero bounces; #476 (PR #478) then ran the same shape and surfaced a spec divergence in its plan comment rather than mid-flight. Those figures are the session task ledger's as read at the time; a lane whose figures were not captured records 'not captured' here rather than an estimate. WHAT EVERY LANE REPORT FEEDS THIS KEY: tokens, tool uses, wall-clock, touchpoint count, bounce count, review-pass cost, and the terminal STATUS. The first PARTIAL, BLOCKED or STRUGGLING ticket is the measurement the pilot lacks — both pilot tickets went clean, so the lane's behaviour when a ticket goes sideways is unpriced. The lane's stop-trigger constants rest on that same gap: owner decision 2026-09-10 (#468), verbatim: 'Stop-trigger constants accepted as provisional (two distinct fixes / two re-plans / two FIX bounces), recorded as provisional in costEvidence.' Their carriers are .claude/agents/ticket-agent.md rule 5 and the ticket-agent lane's step 3 in .claude/skills/run-issue/SKILL.md; the first sideways ticket trues them.
orchestration.delegatedContract: What a BATCH's delegated run owes is unchanged: the evidence templates and the PLAN CHECKPOINT / TASK REPORT / RETRO HANDOVER contract in .claude/agents/task-orchestrator.md. The 2026-08-10 runs on #334, #321 and #200 each released through a RETRO HANDOVER comment that this retro consumed as its first-hand input and found sufficient — that is the contract half of the delegated-pilot graduation bar, met. (Whether each ran on the real agent type or on a general-purpose agent reading the contract from disk is not recorded in the handovers; the contract is a file, so fidelity held either way.) What did NOT graduate is the per-single-issue lane, and it failed on cost rather than on fidelity. What a TICKET-AGENT run owes is the plan comment and the '## Lane report', both specified in .claude/agents/ticket-agent.md.
orchestration.modeHistory: Superseded values, kept so an older reference resolves: 'flat' = everything inline; 'delegated-pilot' = /run-issue on selected issues while the owner evaluated; 'delegated' = /run-issue on every issue; 'batch-delegated' = single issues inline, same-surface batches delegated. 'ticket-agent' keeps that batch half and replaces its inline half with one agent per issue.
orchestration.rollback: Roll back to 'batch-delegated' if a lane-merged PR is reverted for a defect whose docs/review-feedback.md entry names a standard the lane's reviewer pass should have caught, or if a lane report is shown to have declared DONE over an unmet criterion — those two are what the lane's structure can produce and the shape it replaced could not, one per independent read it consolidates. Roll forward — dropping the reviewer pass for small source diffs — only on the graduation rule docs/review-feedback.md declares, read over consecutive lane PRs whose review pass returned APPROVE with zero FIX-NOW. The batch half keeps its own trigger: roll it back to 'delegated' if a batch run is found to have shipped a member's work unverified or lost a member silently. Any of these is a retro PR the owner decides.

feedbackLogLedger: Restatement ledger (docs/standards/architecture.md rule 9) for the feedbackLog path, which is the owning declaration above; JSON takes no comments, so the ledger takes this file's own idiom and lives in a sibling key. A FLOOR, NOT A CENSUS: it is what `command grep -rnE 'review-feedback\.md'` over tracked files returned on 2026-08-11, classified — and a path-literal sweep cannot see a paraphrase ('the feedback log'), so a rename re-runs the sweep shaped around the claim rather than trusting this list, and expects to find sites the list omits. Carriers, which state the path and must move with it: in this file, merge.reviewedSourceRule, merge.humanAlwaysRule, merge.mergeRitual and merge.mergeRitualGate; .github/workflows/ci.yml's merge-ritual-gate comment block and its grep step — the executable carrier, so a rename that misses it reddens merge-ritual-gate on every 'awaiting-review' PR with an error naming a file that no longer exists; CLAUDE.md's Merge-policy bullet; .claude/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/run-issue/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/retro/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/plan-issue/SKILL.md; .claude/agents/task-orchestrator.md; docs/design/task-orchestrator.md, docs/design/design-principles.md and docs/design/map-treatment.md. Not carriers: docs/tech-debt.md and docs/friction-log.md hold the path only inside past-tense narration of what specific tickets did, which rule 9 permits and a rename leaves standing.
